checked_obligation: For every positive integer n satisfying (-a)^n ≡ 1 (mod p), prove that (p-1)/2 divides n under the assumption that a is a primitive root modulo p.
reason: Squaring (-a)^n ≡ 1 gives a^(2n) ≡ 1 (mod p). Since a is a primitive root modulo p, ord_p(a)=p-1, so p-1 divides 2n. Writing p-1=2((p-1)/2) and cancelling 2 yields (p-1)/2 divides n. The supplied group-theorem candidates are unnecessary.
